column1: #tags column:3
Convert a power ratio and a voltage ratio to dB.
column2: \(10\log_{10}(P_2/P_1)\) for power; \(20\log_{10}(V_2/V_1)\) for voltage, valid only when both voltages are across equal impedances.

column1: 3 dB, 10 dB and 20 dB as power ratios? As amplitude ratios?
0 dBm, 30 dBm and −30 dBm in watts?
column2: 1 mW, 1 W and 1 µW. dBm is absolute power referenced to 1 mW; never add two dBm values.

column1: How long does \(e^{-t/\tau}\) take to fall to a fraction \(p\)?
column2: \(t = \tau\ln(1/p)\): 0.69τ to half, 2.3τ to 10%, 4.6τ to 1%.

column1: Thermal voltage \(V_T\) at 300 K?
column2: \(V_T = kT/q \approx 25.85\) mV.

column1: Why must the argument of \(e^x\), \(\ln x\) or \(\sin x\) be dimensionless?
column2: Their power series add \(x\), \(x^2\), \(x^3\)…, which only makes sense for a pure number. Write \(e^{-t/\tau}\), \(\ln(I/I_S)\), \(\sin(\omega t)\) with ω in rad/s.

column1: Diode or BJT voltage change per decade of current at room temperature?
column2: \(V_T\ln 10 \approx 59.5\) mV per decade.

column1: How do you recognize exponential vs power-law data on a plot?
column2: Exponential: straight line on semi-log axes (log y vs x). Power law: straight line on log–log axes, with slope = exponent.

column1: 1 rad in degrees; ω for 60 Hz?
column2: 57.30°; \(\omega = 2\pi\cdot60 \approx 377\) rad/s.

column1: Change of base for logarithms?
\(\lim_{x\to0}\sin x/x\)? Where does it matter?
column2: 1 (radians). It gives \(\sin x \approx x\) for small angles and is the key step in differentiating sin.

column1: \(\lim_{n\to\infty}(1 + x/n)^n\)?
column2: \(e^x\): continuous compounding; at \(n = 365\), \((1 + 1/n)^n = 2.715\) vs \(e = 2.718\).

column1: What three conditions make \(f\) continuous at \(a\)?
column2: \(f(a)\) exists, \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) exists, and they are equal.

column1: Which circuit quantities must be continuous at a switching event, and why?
column2: Capacitor voltage and inductor current: a jump would need infinite current (\(i = C\,dv/dt\)) or infinite voltage (\(v = L\,di/dt\)).

column1: How many bisection steps for 3 more decimal digits?
column2: About 10 (\(2^{10} = 1024\)); width after \(n\) steps is \((b - a)/2^n\).

column1: High-frequency behavior of a one-pole low-pass \(1/\sqrt{1 + (f/f_c)^2}\)?
column2: \(\approx f_c/f\): −20 dB/decade, on an asymptote through 0 dB at \(f_c\). The true gain at \(f_c\) is −3.01 dB.

column1: How do you find a limit at infinity of a rational function?
column2: Keep only the leading terms of numerator and denominator: equal degree gives the ratio of coefficients.

column1: What does the intermediate value theorem guarantee?
column2: A continuous function that changes sign on \([a, b]\) has a root there; the basis of bisection.

column1: Why does a forward difference fail for very small \(h\) in floating point?
column2: Round-off: subtracting nearly equal numbers loses digits. Best \(h \approx 10^{-8}\) (≈ √machine epsilon) in double precision.

column1: What does 'settled within 1%' mean for an exponential, and after how long?
column2: \(e^{-t/\tau} < 0.01\), i.e. after 4.6τ; after 5τ it is within 0.7%.

column1: Definition of the derivative?
column2: \(f'(x) = \lim_{h\to0}\big(f(x + h) - f(x)\big)/h\): the slope of the tangent, the instantaneous rate.

column1: Chain rule?
Product and quotient rules?
Capacitor and inductor laws?
column2: \(i = C\,dv/dt\); \(v = L\,di/dt\). 1 µF at 1 V/µs draws 1 A; 1 µH at 1 A/µs develops 1 V.

column1: Small-signal resistance of a diode at 1 mA?
column2: \(r_d = V_T/I \approx 26\ \Omega\); it halves when the current doubles.

column1: Derivative of \(\sin(\omega t)\)?
column2: \(\omega\cos(\omega t)\): differentiation multiplies a sinusoid's amplitude by ω and advances its phase 90°.

column1: What is slew rate, and how does it limit full-power bandwidth?
column2: The maximum \(dv/dt\) of an amplifier output. A sine of peak \(V_p\) needs \(\omega V_p\), so \(f_{max} = SR/(2\pi V_p)\).

column1: Implicit differentiation of \(I = I_S(e^{V/V_T} - 1)\)?
column2: \(dV/dI = V_T/(I + I_S) \approx V_T/I\).

column1: Why is the central difference better than the forward difference?
column2: Its error is \(\propto h^2\), not \(h\), so it reaches higher accuracy at a larger, round-off-safe step (≈ 10⁻⁵).

column1: Is \(\lvert x\rvert\) differentiable at 0?
column2: No: the left and right slopes (−1 and +1) differ. Continuity does not imply differentiability.

column1: How do you classify a critical point in one variable?
column2: \(f' = 0\); \(f'' > 0\) minimum, \(f'' < 0\) maximum, \(f'' = 0\) inconclusive. Always check endpoints too.

column1: Maximum power transfer condition and value?
column2: \(R_L = R_s\); \(P_{max} = V_s^2/(4R_s)\), with only 50% efficiency. Used for signals, not power delivery.

column1: How much power is lost with a 2× load mismatch?
column2: About 11% (89% of \(P_{max}\)) either way: optima are flat because the slope is zero there.

column1: Minimum of \(ax + b/x\)?
column2: At \(x = \sqrt{b/a}\), value \(2\sqrt{ab}\); the two terms are equal at the optimum.

column1: Linearization formula and its error?
column2: \(f(x_0 + \Delta x) \approx f(x_0) + f'(x_0)\Delta x\); error is second order, \(\tfrac12f''\Delta x^2\). This is the small-signal idea.

column1: Newton's method update?
column2: \(x_{k+1} = x_k - g(x_k)/g'(x_k)\); digits roughly double per step near a simple root, but it can diverge from a poor start.

column1: How does SPICE find a DC operating point, and how does it keep Newton from diverging?
column2: Newton's method on the nonlinear circuit equations, with damping and step limiting (capping the voltage change per iteration).

column1: When does L'Hôpital's rule apply?
column2: Only to 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms: then \(\lim f/g = \lim f'/g'\).

column1: How small must a signal be for the diode small-signal model?
column2: Swing ≪ \(V_T\) ≈ 26 mV; about 10% error at 5 mV.

column1: What does the mean value theorem say?
column2: Somewhere in \((a, b)\), \(f'(c) = \big(f(b) - f(a)\big)/(b - a)\): the average rate is attained at some instant.

column1: Fundamental theorem of calculus?
column2: \(\int_a^b f\,dx = F(b) - F(a)\) where \(F' = f\); and \(\frac{d}{dx}\int_a^x f\,dt = f(x)\).

column1: Charge from current; energy from power?
column2: \(q = \int i\,dt\); \(w = \int p\,dt\). 1 Ah = 3600 C; 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ.

column1: Capacitor voltage from its current?
Energy lost charging a capacitor from a fixed source through R?
column2: \(\tfrac12CV^2\), whatever R: half the \(CV^2\) the source delivers.

column1: Area under \(Ae^{-t/\tau}\) from 0 to ∞?
column2: \(A\tau\): the 'equivalent rectangle'.

column1: Average of a full-wave and half-wave rectified sine of peak \(V_m\)?
column2: \(2V_m/\pi \approx 0.637V_m\) and \(V_m/\pi \approx 0.318V_m\).

column1: Average of \(\sin^2\) over a period?
column2: ½, which is why \(P = \tfrac12I_m^2R\) and RMS uses √2.

column1: Ideal op-amp integrator output?
column2: \(v_{out} = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_{in}\,dt\); a square wave in gives a triangle wave out.

column1: Trapezoid vs Simpson error orders?
column2: \(h^2\) vs \(h^4\): halving h cuts the error to ¼ vs 1/16.

column1: Why integrate over 16.67 ms or 20 ms in precision meters?
column2: A whole number of mains periods (60 / 50 Hz): the integral of the hum is then zero.

column1: Why does a coulomb-counting fuel gauge drift?
column2: Integration accumulates a constant sensor offset forever; gauges recalibrate at known states (full charge, rested open-circuit voltage).

column1: Integration by parts?
column2: \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\); pick \(u\) that simplifies when differentiated (LIATE).

column1: \(\int_0^\infty t^ne^{-t}dt\)?
column2: \(n!\); so \(\int_0^\infty te^{-t/\tau}dt = \tau^2\).

column1: Orthogonality of sines over one period?
column2: \(\int_0^T\sin(m\omega t)\sin(n\omega t)dt = 0\) for \(m \ne n\), \(T/2\) for \(m = n\): the basis of Fourier series.

column1: Noise bandwidth of a one-pole low-pass?
column2: \((\pi/2)f_c \approx 1.571f_c\): 57% more noise power than \(f_c\) suggests.

column1: Thermal noise of 1 kΩ at 300 K?
column2: \(\sqrt{4kTR} \approx 4.07\) nV/√Hz; scales as √R.

column1: kT/C noise at 1 pF and 300 K?
column2: \(\sqrt{kT/C} \approx 64.3\) µV rms, independent of R.

column1: Fourier fundamental of a ±A square wave?
column2: \((4/\pi)A \approx 1.273A\), carrying 81% of the power; harmonics \(4A/(n\pi)\) for odd n.

column1: When does \(\int_1^\infty x^{-p}dx\) converge?
column2: Only for \(p > 1\). At \(p = 1\) (1/f noise) every decade carries equal power.

column1: Partial fractions: what do you do first if the degree of the numerator ≥ the denominator's?
column2: Polynomial long division; then split the proper remainder into simple fractions.

column1: Elmore delay vs 50% delay for a single pole?
column2: Elmore = τ; 50% delay = τ ln 2; ratio 1.443.

column1: Definition of RMS?
column2: \(V_{rms} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{T}\int_0^Tv^2dt}\): the DC voltage that heats a resistor equally.

column1: RMS of sine, square and triangle (peak \(V_p\))?
PWM at duty D and peak \(V_p\): average and RMS?
column2: Average \(DV_p\); RMS \(\sqrt{D}V_p\).

column1: RMS of DC plus ripple?
column2: \(\sqrt{V_{dc}^2 + V_{ac,rms}^2}\): orthogonal parts add in quadrature.

column1: Average AC power with phase angle φ?
column2: \(P = V_{rms}I_{rms}\cos\varphi = \tfrac12V_pI_p\cos\varphi\).

column1: Usable energy of a capacitor discharged from \(V_1\) to \(V_1/2\)?
column2: 75% of \(\tfrac12CV_1^2\), because energy goes as \(V^2\).

column1: Gaussian coverage within ±1σ, ±2σ, ±3σ?
RMS quantization error of an ideal ADC?
column2: \(\Delta/\sqrt{12} \approx 0.29\) LSB, from the variance of a uniform density.

column1: Ideal N-bit ADC SNR for a full-scale sine?
column2: \(6.02N + 1.76\) dB; 12 bits gives 74.0 dB.

column1: What does an MTBF of 1,000,000 h mean?
column2: About one failure per million device-hours across a fleet (≈ 114 device-years), not a lifetime of one unit.

column1: Geometric series sum?
column2: \(\sum_{k\ge0}r^k = 1/(1 - r)\) for \(\lvert r\rvert < 1\); e.g. the DC gain of \(y[n] = ry[n-1] + x[n]\).

column1: Does the harmonic series converge?
column2: No: \(\sum 1/k\) grows like \(\ln n\) (≈ 14.4 at 10⁶ terms). \(\sum 1/k^2 = \pi^2/6\) converges.

column1: Taylor series of \(f\) about \(a\)?
column2: \(\sum f^{(n)}(a)(x - a)^n/n!\), valid inside its radius of convergence.

column1: Maclaurin series of \(e^x\), \(\sin x\), \(\cos x\)?
Lagrange remainder?
column2: \(R_n = f^{(n+1)}(\xi)(x - a)^{n+1}/(n + 1)!\) for some ξ between a and x; bound it by the largest value of \(f^{(n+1)}\).

column1: Alternating-series error bound?
column2: For alternating terms shrinking to 0, the error is less than the first omitted term.

column1: Small-angle error of \(\sin x \approx x\) at 0.1 rad?
Closed-loop gain error from finite loop gain?
column2: \(G = A/(1 + A\beta) \approx (1/\beta)(1 - 1/(A\beta))\): relative error ≈ 1/loop gain.

column1: HD2 and HD3 from Taylor coefficients?
column2: HD2 ≈ \(\frac{a_2}{2a_1}A\); HD3 ≈ \(\frac{a_3}{4a_1}A^2\). HD2 rises 20 dB and HD3 40 dB per decade of amplitude.

column1: HD2 of an exponential device for 1 mV input?
Partial derivative \(\partial f/\partial x\)?
column2: The rate of change of f with x, holding all other variables fixed.

column1: Total differential?
column2: \(df = f_x\,dx + f_y\,dy\): the linear sensitivity to small changes in all inputs.

column1: Worst-case vs RSS tolerance stacking?
column2: Worst case adds \(\lvert\)sensitivity × tolerance\(\rvert\); RSS adds them in quadrature, for independent errors.

column1: What does the gradient tell you?
column2: Its direction is steepest ascent, its length the steepest rate, and it is perpendicular to level curves.

column1: Directional derivative?
column2: \(D_{\mathbf u}f = \nabla f\cdot\mathbf u\) for a unit vector u.

column1: Second-derivative test in two variables?
Lagrange condition and the meaning of λ?
column2: \(\nabla f = \lambda\nabla g\) on \(g = c\); λ is the change in the optimal value per unit of constraint (a shadow price).

column1: Elasticities of CMOS dynamic power \(P = \alpha CV^2f\)?
column2: 2 in V and 1 in f; 3 together when V scales with f (DVFS).

column1: Square-law MOSFET \(g_m\)?
column2: \(g_m = 2I_D/(V_{GS} - V_{TH})\); intrinsic gain \(g_mr_o \approx 2V_A/V_{ov}\).

column1: Gradient-descent stability limit?
column2: Step \(\eta < 2/\lambda_{max}\) of the Hessian; a large condition number makes convergence slow.

column1: Area and volume elements in polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates?
column2: \(r\,dr\,d\theta\); \(r\,dr\,d\theta\,dz\); \(\rho^2\sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta\). Never forget the Jacobian.

column1: \(\int_{-\infty}^\infty e^{-x^2}dx\)?
column2: \(\sqrt\pi \approx 1.772\), found by squaring and switching to polar coordinates.

column1: What does Fubini's theorem allow?
column2: Evaluating a double integral as nested single integrals in either order; swapping the order can make a hard integral easy.

column1: What makes a vector field conservative?
column2: Line integrals depend only on endpoints ⇔ \(\mathbf F = \nabla\varphi\) ⇔ curl-free on a region without holes. That is why voltage is well defined in electrostatics.

column1: Divergence and curl, physically?
column2: Divergence: net outflow per unit volume (source density). Curl: circulation per unit area (rotation).

column1: Divergence theorem and Stokes' theorem?
column2: Flux out of a closed surface = ∭ div F dV. Circulation around a loop = flux of curl F through any surface it bounds.

column1: Gauss's law and Ampère's law (static)?
column2: \(\oint\mathbf E\cdot d\mathbf A = Q_{enc}/\varepsilon_0\); \(\oint\mathbf B\cdot d\mathbf l = \mu_0I_{enc}\).

column1: Magnetic field 1 cm from a 1 A wire?
Copper skin depth at 100 kHz and 1 MHz?
column2: \(\delta = \sqrt{\rho/(\pi f\mu_0)}\): about 0.21 mm and 0.066 mm.

column1: Dies-per-wafer formula, and why do big dies cost more than proportionally?
column2: \(\pi d^2/(4A) - \pi d/\sqrt{2A}\). Edge loss grows in relative size and yield \(e^{-AD_0}\) falls exponentially with area.
